title: Eigenvalues (−1 ± i√3)/2: a decaying oscillation
caption: The Jacobian has trace −1 and determinant 1, so the eigenvalues are (−1 ± i√3)/2: the imaginary part makes x(t) oscillate and the negative real part makes the oscillation die away as e^(−t/2).
alt: The position x against time for the system starting at x = 1: a wave that crosses zero repeatedly and shrinks inside the dashed decay envelope e to the minus t over 2.
description: The Jacobian [[0, 1], [−1, −1]] has trace −1 and determinant 1.
Its eigenvalues (−1 ± i√3)/2 have real part −½ and imaginary part ±√3/2.
A solution from x(0) = 1, y(0) = 0 is x = e^(−t/2)(cos(√3t/2) + sin(√3t/2)/√3).
It oscillates (imaginary part) and decays (negative real part): a stable spiral.

checks.name: the envelope decays at the real part −½: e^(−1) at t = 2
